2.  Observe the code used to load in the iris dataset. Explain what the header and col.names arguments do.

```{r}
# IMPORTANT: You do not need to change anything in this chunk. Just run it!
url <- "https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/iris/iris.data"
# For reference
iris_df <- read.csv(url, header = FALSE, 
                    col.names = c("Sepal.Length",
                                  "Sepal.Width",
                                  "Petal.Length", 
                                  "Petal.Width", 
                                  "Species"))
```

**Answer:** *Delete this text and type in your answer.*

3.  Extract the `Sepal.Length` column from the iris dataset in two different ways.

**Indexing by brackets**:
```{r}
# Use the data_frame_name[row, column] syntax
# We want to retrieve ALL rows, but only the Sepal.Length column
# Save the values under the column to the object sepal_len
sepal_len <- iris_df[..., ...]

# Use head() to print out the first few rows of the object
head(sepal_len)
```

**Indexing by the** **`$`** **operator**:
```{r}
# Use the data_frame_name$column_name syntax
# Save the values under the column to the object sepal_len
sepal_len <- iris_df$...

# Use head() to print out the first few rows of the object
head(sepal_len)
```
